《人，你可以倚靠鸟的胸膛》作者：星愉

文案：

白粼粼，一遭车祸死了，转生成了一只二手市场的和尚鹦鹉。

好消息：他终于不用上那个破班了，啾啾啾啾！

坏消息：他因为不会学舌，马上就要被“处理”了。

店老板直接打算捉他，白粼粼当机立断乱飞一气，啪唧一头撞上一个少年怀里。

“欸！”

白粼粼啾啾乱叫，蓝毛乱飞，假装自己腿瘸了，俨然碰瓷了起来。

老板也不知道何时默契了起来，当即就讹上了。

“你弄伤了我的鸟，你要赔偿，最低得五百——“

“我买了。“

阴郁的少年掏出手机就付了款，白粼粼站在他的肩膀上，跟他回了家。

*

宋郁孤僻又厌世，手腕上是一道道的疤痕，他从花鸟市场上带回来一只鸟。

原本是想放生，但又怕它死，只好先放在家里。

去厨房，小鸟飞到他肩膀上，“啾啾啾”

“……”

去写作业，小鸟叽叽歪歪啄纸条，“啾啾啾”

“……”

去洗手间，小鸟大摇大摆要跟着去，“啾啾啾.”

宋郁砰得关上门，把鸟撞得眼冒金星。

他连自己都养不了，怎么养鸟，宋郁躺在床上，修长的手指盖住眼睛。

电脑屏幕上的游戏还开着，他耳朵嗡嗡鸣鸣的，听不清楚。

不知何时睡了过去。

再度醒来的时候……

“啾啾啾，煞笔队友，不许挂机！”

“啾啾，去死啊！我一大炮轰死你。”

宋郁从床上坐直了身子，头发都被压翘了，面色恍惚。

白粼粼一个爪子踹开了鼠标，生气极了，砰砰跳跳地回头。

“……”

“……”

男生捂了捂脸，而后呆呆地看着它，自言自语道，“你是鹦鹉，会说话很正常。”

白粼粼松了一口气。

但下一秒。

“但鹦鹉还会打游戏的么？”

*

白粼粼自从来了宋家，就十分满意，别的不说，这大别墅，深得鸟满意。

宋郁一上学，他就熟练地用鸟爪打开电脑打游戏。

偶尔用喙撬开冰箱，给自己补偿点美食。

他是后来才发现自己不同于其他小鸟的，他可以吃人类的食物，正他日渐圆润的时候。

窗外飞来了一只信鸽。

——白粼粼，妖怪编号247，尚未化形，贫困补助已到。

说罢就留下一个信封。

白粼粼用喙叼过来了那张纸，但刚看完纸张就化成了灰烬，一股力量注入了体内。

它的身躯开始一点点变大，爪子甚至在地板上滑出了痕迹。

膨到了一米多高，但……仍然没有化形。

宋郁一开门，巨大的鸟就在他的房间，羽毛蓬松，胸膛挺立。

他大抵是病得更重了。

白粼粼犹豫了下，张开了翅膀，迟疑地问他，“要、要埋一下吗？”

==小鸡很爱你==

==萌宠文==

高亮：攻是高中生，实际上是年下，后期有病的那种，占有欲比较高。

连载防盗已开，百分之七十。

弃文不必告知，本文不包饺子，没有副cp。

*Human, You Can Lean on a Bird's Chest*
Author: Xing Yu

**Synopsis:**

Bai Linlin died in a car accident and transmigrated into a second-hand Quaker parrot in a pet market.

The good news: He finally didn't have to go to that crappy job anymore! *Chirp chirp chirp chirp!*

The bad news: Because he couldn't mimic human speech, he was about to be "disposed of."

When the shop owner lunged to catch him, Bai Linlin made a split-second decision to fly around wildly, crashing headfirst right into a young boy's chest.

"Whoa!"

Bai Linlin chirped frantically, his blue feathers flying everywhere. He pretended his leg was broken, shamelessly staging a scam to cling to the boy.

The shop owner, displaying an unexpected and sudden synergy, immediately seized the opportunity to extort the kid.

"You injured my bird! You have to compensate me. At least five hundred—"

"I'll buy it."

The gloomy youth pulled out his phone and paid on the spot. Bai Linlin perched on his shoulder and went home with him.

*

Song Yu was antisocial and world-weary, his wrists lined with scars. He had brought a bird back from the flower and bird market.

Initially, he wanted to release it, but fearing it would die, he had no choice but to keep it at home for the time being.

When he went to the kitchen, the little bird flew onto his shoulder. "Chirp chirp."

"..."

When he sat down to do his homework, the little bird pecked at his papers, making a racket. "Chirp chirp."

"..."

When he went to the bathroom, the little bird strutted along, insisting on following him. "Chirp chirp."

Song Yu slammed the door shut, leaving the bird seeing stars from bumping into it.

He couldn't even take care of himself, so how was he supposed to raise a bird? Song Yu lay on his bed, covering his eyes with his slender fingers.

The game on his computer screen was still running. His ears buzzed, and he couldn't hear clearly.

Without realizing it, he drifted off to sleep.

When he woke up again...

"Chirp chirp chirp! Brain-dead teammate, don't you dare go AFK!"

"Chirp chirp! Go die! I'll blast you to pieces with my cannon!"

Song Yu sat straight up in bed, his hair messy from sleep, a dazed expression on his face.

Bai Linlin kicked the mouse away with one claw. Furious, he hopped around and turned his head.

"..."

"..."

The boy covered his face, then stared blankly at the bird, muttering to himself, "You're a parrot. It's normal for you to talk."

Bai Linlin let out a sigh of relief.

But in the next second:

"But do parrots play video games too?"

*

Ever since Bai Linlin arrived at the Song residence, he had been extremely satisfied. If nothing else, this massive villa was highly approved of by the bird.

As soon as Song Yu went to school, he would skillfully use his claws to turn on the computer and play games.

Occasionally, he would pry open the refrigerator with his beak to reward himself with some human delicacies.

It was only later that he realized he was different from other birds. He could eat human food, and just as he was growing rounder by the day...

A carrier pigeon flew in through the window.

—*Bai Linlin, Monster No. 247. Un-transformed. Your poverty subsidy has arrived.*

With that, it dropped an envelope.

Bai Linlin picked up the paper with his beak, but as soon as he finished reading it, the paper turned to ash, and a surge of power poured into his body.

His body began to expand bit by bit, his claws even leaving scratch marks on the floor.

He swelled to over a meter tall, but... he still hadn't transformed into a human.

When Song Yu opened the door, a giant bird was sitting in his room, its feathers fluffy and its chest proudly puffed out.

He must be getting sicker.

Bai Linlin hesitated, spread his wings, and asked tentatively, "Do... do you want to bury yourself in them?"

== The little bird loves you very much ==
== Cute pet novel ==

Highlight: The male lead is a high school student, actually younger than the protagonist (年下). He gets a bit unstable later on, with high possessiveness.
Serialized anti-theft is set to 70%.
No need to announce if you drop the novel. This story does not force a happy ending for everyone, and there are no side couples.
The first half focuses more on the male lead's plot, while the second half focuses on the Bird King's plot.
(Sending hearts)
The author drew the character art themselves, just for the writing chicken to play with~
The little chicken on the cover isn't it, but the rest are drawn by me.

第1章

“这鸟是个智障。”

嘈杂的花鸟市场里人来人往的，一个光头大叔坐在躺椅上，翘着二郎腿，一锤定音道。

这家小店其貌不扬，但里面放着大大小小数十个笼子，各种各样颜色的小鸟在木头栖干上梳理羽毛，发出此起彼伏的拟人叫声。

“智障！智障！”

一只玄凤头顶的呆毛动了动，很是通人性地飞到了店老板的肩头，也对着小茶几一个呆头呆脑、脑袋浑圆的蓝羽和尚鹦鹉学舌道。

玄凤早就看它不爽了。

不就是个近几年引入的品种，老家在……在那个南、南美洲。

它早年也是外国鸟，可它骄傲了吗？

隔壁的牡丹、虎皮也都是好鸟，大家身价都差不多，这才合群好不好。

凭什么这新来的身价要四位数！!

王侯鸟相，宁有种乎！

玄凤气得腮红都变得鲜艳了几分，正所谓输给强者理所应当，输给智障简直是耻辱万分。

但店老板也有点不死心，手里还盘着两个核桃，微微往前弯了下腰，甚至还拿手戳了下呆鸟，喃喃道：

“这，总不能真有点问题吧，还能飞成直线吗？”

“啧，不过这品种的不都是很吵得么？难不成这还是个哑巴？”

呆鸟被戳了也不为所动，脑袋圆圆的，蓬松的羽毛几乎挡住了绿豆一样的眼睛。

只是挪动了下位置，爪子还打了下滑。

店老板：“……”

他今年总共就进了一批蓝羽的和尚，这小东西圆头圆脑的，今年市场尤为喜爱，价格也水涨船高。

本来还指望大赚一笔，结果也不知道是家庭繁育出问题了还是怎么的，一窝成活的不多，挑挑拣拣留下来个品相最好的。

结果死活不会叫。

呆得跟个发条鸟一样。

最后店老板也是叹了口气，像是彻底放弃，躺回了椅子上，自言自语道：

“这一看就是有病的。”

白粼粼本来都已经完全失去了意识，在卡车撞过来的一瞬间，怨念十足的社畜灵魂一下子抽离体外。

那种虚无的感觉还没有持续多久。

就听到了这么一句话。

艹！

——你有病！你全家都有病！

——死老板，死同事，老子变成恶鬼咬死你们！

白粼粼怨念十足、甚至可以想象到自己周身黑气涌动，最好是阴森森的，这样子看谁还敢奴役他！

但实际情况是一只肥嘟嘟、圆不溜秋的呆鸟突然扑棱翅膀，开始大声怪叫：

“啾啾啾！啾啾啾啾啾啾！”

“啾啾啾啾啾啾……”

小门店被吵得震天响，店老板甚至直接心悸了，从躺椅上起身，颤颤巍巍抬手在茶几上拿了个速效救心丸。

“我去，这、这鸟，我养着真是要短命。”

男人抬手拿了保温杯，很是费劲巴拉地仰头吞服了药丸，心想坏了。

真是还不如智障呢？

这成疯鸟了，还能卖吗？

茶几上的“发条鸟”此刻像是零件重组了一样，脑袋歪了歪，在桌面上蹦跶，一会活动下鸟腿，一会扑棱翅膀。

反正像是抽风。

店老板深吸一口气，下定了决心，折价不折价都无所谓了。

得赶紧出手，不然真亏个底朝天。

而与此同时——

白粼粼一脸懵，他的视线很低，只能看到放大了数倍的茶几、椅子、还有……人。

由于店门是开着的，临着路，人来人往的，而且这时候似乎是中午放学了，还有抄近道骑单车回家的学生。

各种各样的市井声音传来。

他好久没有看到白天的太阳了，因为上班通勤要一个半小时，天都不大亮，自己就要上工了。

呸！

白粼粼越想越生气，恨不得立刻就去找那死上司，咔咔咬死他。

不过现在……很明显有另一件事需要处理。

他低头看了看自己的身躯，视线里是毛绒绒的羽毛，胸膛挺立。

“……”

[这是哪里？]

“啾啾啾啾？”

白粼粼这才接受一个事实，他转生成了只鸟，而且不会说人话。

他刚刚的高攻击性造成的炸毛还暂时没有消退，在桌子上蹦跶了几下，环顾了四周。

[哎呀哎呀，你看它。]

[它好凶啊，是不是所有公鸟都这样？]

[能不能别吵了，看不见老娘在孵蛋吗！]

这个小小的店面，容纳着将近百来只小鸟，挤在一起更是七嘴八舌的。

有个栖杆甚至排排站着好几只鸟，分别是……生芒果、半生不熟芒果、熟透了的芒果。

“……”

白粼粼这才确定，自己无师自通了鸟语，而且是高级一些的“鹦语”。

不过这都不重要。

刚才谁骂他智障的！

白粼粼很快接受了自己的身份，人是不能飞的，但鸟可就不存在这种问题了。

桌子上的蓝色和尚身躯下压，羽毛蓬松，俨然是个雄赳赳气昂昂的起飞状态。

玄凤在木头栖干上莫名有些紧张，朝左边挪了下位置。

但就在白粼粼试图“大鹏展翅”的时候，一个阴影覆了过来，鸟被一下子握住了。

只余鸟头转动。

施法失败。

“对，十分钟后上门吧，没问题的，纯种和尚的。”

白粼粼感觉自己被转了转了，那秃头店老板倒是又仔细打量了下，接着打电话道：

“看你说的，我这是纯纯亏本，相当于直接送你一只公鸟。”

“其他店光是配种一次都收多少钱呢？这你拿去可以一直配。”

“就五百块，过了这村就没这店了……”

白粼粼震惊地瞪大了鸟眼，配种？一直配？才五百块？

他毕竟还是个人的芯子。

完全接受不了这么赤裸的鸟体交易。

于是乎。

在店老板沉浸在自己把一只病鸟卖了这么个好价钱的喜悦中，虎口突然一阵刺痛，皮肉一下子被叨开了。

他本能地松了下手。

蓝色小鸟蹭得一下飞了起来，这还多亏了原先比较呆，店老板也就没有剪羽。

小店里“鸡”飞蛋打。

秃头老板疼得龇牙咧嘴的，但很快邪火就上来了，试图逮回来乱飞的鸟。

白粼粼刚做鸟还不太熟练，小店又实在是发挥空间有限，他只能在躲避那个竹竿的同时，使劲朝着门口飞。

自由！

自由！

眼下正值十二点，南城一高的学生也陆陆续续地开始回家，人来人往的。

不仅有单车，还有电瓶车，甚至还有滑板少年。

危险指数翻倍。

但白粼粼压根没意识到这个，反正他绝对不会去配种的，大不了出去找点虫子吃，蛋白质还高！

他一股脑地飞了出去。

“欸！这死鸟！”

白粼粼感受到了风、炸串的香……以及淡雅的薰衣草……

洗衣液的味道？

啪唧。

鸟来不及刹车了，撞上了一个路过的高中生，正在白粼粼重心不稳要摔的时候。

少年垂眸稳稳地用手托住了。

人与鸟对视。

白粼粼不由得啾了几声。

[我去，小奶狗。]

Chapter 1 (Part 1)

"This bird is brain-damaged."

In the bustling, noisy flower and bird market, people bustled to and fro. A bald middle-aged man sat on a reclining chair, legs crossed, delivering his final verdict.

His little shop was unremarkable, but it housed dozens of cages of various sizes. Birds of all colors preened their feathers on wooden perches, letting out a chorus of human-like mimicry.

"Brain-damaged! Brain-damaged!"

The crest of a cockatiel twitched. Displaying quite a bit of human-like intelligence, it flew onto the shop owner's shoulder and mimicked his words, pointing its head at a round-headed, blue-feathered Quaker parrot sitting on the small tea table.

The cockatiel had disliked this newcomer for a long time.

So what if it was a breed introduced in recent years, whose ancestral home was in... in South, South America?

It was a foreign bird in its early years too, but did it brag?

The lovebirds and budgies next door were all good birds, and everyone's value was about the same. That was what made them a crowd.

Why did this newcomer have a four-digit price tag?!

Are noble birds born to their high stations?!

The cockatiel's rosy cheeks flushed a bit brighter with anger. As the saying went, losing to the strong was only natural, but losing to a brain-damaged fool was an absolute disgrace.

But the shop owner was still reluctant to give up. Rolling two walnuts in his hand, he leaned forward slightly and even poked the dazed bird with his finger, muttering:

"Surely there can't really be something wrong with it, right? Can it even fly in a straight line?"

"Tsk, but aren't birds of this breed usually very noisy? Don't tell me this one is a mute?"

The dazed bird remained unmoved even after being poked. Its head was perfectly round, and its fluffy feathers almost completely obscured its tiny, bead-like eyes.

It merely shifted its position slightly, its claws slipping a bit on the table.

The shop owner: "..."

He had only imported one batch of blue Quaker parrots this year. These little things had round heads and round bodies, which the market particularly adored this year, causing their prices to skyrocket.

He had hoped to make a fortune, but for some reason—perhaps a breeding issue—not many from the clutch survived. After careful selection, he was left with this one, which had the best appearance.

Yet, it refused to make a single sound.

It was as stiff and lifeless as a wind-up toy.

Finally, the shop owner let out a sigh, seemingly giving up entirely. He leaned back into his chair and muttered to himself:

"This one is definitely sick."

Bai Linlin had completely lost consciousness earlier. The moment the truck crashed into him, his resentment-filled soul of a corporate slave had been instantly ripped from his body.

That feeling of nothingness hadn't lasted long.

Before he heard those words.

Damn it!

—*You're the one who's sick! Your whole family is sick!*

—*Deadbeat boss, deadbeat colleagues, I'll turn into an evil spirit and bite you all to death!*

Filled with resentment, Bai Linlin could almost picture dark energy swirling around him, looking as sinister as possible. Let's see who would dare enslave him then!

But the reality was that a plump, round, dazed bird suddenly flapped its wings and began to screech at the top of its lungs:

"Chirp chirp chirp! Chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp!"

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp..."

The small shop was filled with a deafening racket. The shop owner's heart skipped a beat. He scrambled up from his reclining chair and tremblingly reached for a fast-acting heart pill from the tea table.

"My god, keeping this... this bird is really going to shorten my life."

The man picked up his thermos, tilted his head back with great effort, and swallowed the pill, thinking that things had gone south.

Wasn't this even worse than being brain-damaged?

It had turned into a crazy bird. Could it still be sold?

The "wind-up bird" on the tea table now looked as if its parts had been reassembled. It tilted its head, hopping around on the table, stretching its legs one moment and flapping its wings the next.

In short, it looked like it was having a fit.

Taking a deep breath, the shop owner made up his mind. It didn't matter if he had to sell it at a discount.

He had to get rid of it quickly, or he would lose everything.

Meanwhile—

Bai Linlin was utterly bewildered. His line of sight was extremely low; he could only see a tea table, chairs, and... people, all magnified several times.

Since the shop door was open and faced the street, people were constantly passing by. It seemed to be the noon school dismissal, and some students were taking shortcuts home on their bicycles.

All sorts of bustling street sounds drifted in.

He hadn't seen the sun during the day in a long time. Because his daily commute took an hour and a half, he had to start working before the sun even fully rose.

Pah!

The more Bai Linlin thought about it, the angrier he got. He wished he could find his deadbeat boss right now and bite him to death.

But right now... there was clearly another matter that needed his attention.

He looked down at his own body. In his field of vision were fluffy feathers and a puffed-out chest.

"..."

*Where is this?*

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp?"

Only then did Bai Linlin accept the fact: he had transmigrated into a bird, and he couldn't speak human language.

The fluffiness caused by his high aggressiveness earlier hadn't faded yet. He hopped around on the table a few times, surveying his surroundings.

*Oh my, look at him.*

*He's so fierce. Are all male birds like this?*

*Can you stop making so much noise? Can't you see I'm hatching eggs here!*

This tiny shop housed nearly a hundred small birds, and squeezed together, they were all chirping at once.

On one perch, several birds were standing in a neat row, looking like... raw mangoes, half-ripe mangoes, and fully ripe mangoes.

"..."

Only then did Bai Linlin realize that he had instinctively mastered bird language—specifically, a more advanced "Parrot-ese."

But none of that mattered.

Who called him brain-damaged just now?!

Bai Linlin quickly accepted his new identity. Humans couldn't fly, but birds didn't have that limitation.

The blue Quaker parrot on the table lowered its body, its feathers puffing up, clearly in a majestic, ready-to-fly stance.

The cockatiel on the wooden perch felt inexplicably tense and shifted to the left.

But just as Bai Linlin was about to "spread his wings like a giant Roc," a shadow loomed over him, and he was suddenly grabbed.

Only his bird head could still turn.

The spell had failed.

"Yes, come over in ten minutes. No problem, it's a purebred Quaker."

Bai Linlin felt himself being turned around. The bald shop owner inspected him closely again, then continued on the phone:

"Look at what you're saying. I'm selling this at a pure loss, basically giving you a male bird for free."

"Other shops charge so much just for a single breeding session. You can keep this one for breeding forever."

"Just five hundred yuan. You won't find another deal like this..."

Bai Linlin's bird eyes widened in shock. Breeding? Breeding forever? And for only five hundred yuan?

He still had a human soul, after all.

He absolutely could not accept such a blatant transaction of his avian body.

Thus, while the shop owner was immersed in the joy of selling a sick bird for such a good price, a sudden sharp pain shot through his hand. His skin was instantly nipped open.

Instinctively, he loosened his grip.

The little blue bird shot up into the air. Thanks to its previous dazed state, the shop owner hadn't clipped its wings.

Chaos erupted in the small shop, with feathers and birdseed flying everywhere.

The bald owner grimaced in pain, but anger quickly flared up. He tried to catch the wild-flying bird.

As a new bird, Bai Linlin wasn't very skilled yet, and the small shop offered limited space to maneuver. He could only dodge the bamboo pole while desperately flying toward the entrance.

Freedom!

Freedom!

It was exactly twelve o'clock, and the students of Nancheng No. 1 High School were heading home one after another, creating a steady flow of people.

There were not only bicycles but also electric scooters, and even teenagers on skateboards.

The danger level doubled.

But Bai Linlin didn't care about any of that. In any case, he would absolutely not become a breeding bird. At worst, he would go outside and find some bugs to eat—they were high in protein anyway!

He flew out headlong.

"Hey! You damn bird!"

Bai Linlin felt the wind, the aroma of fried skewers... and a faint, elegant scent of lavender...

The smell of laundry detergent?

*Smack.*

The bird couldn't brake in time and crashed right into a passing high school student. Just as Bai Linlin lost his balance and was about to fall, the youth looked down and caught him steadily in his hands.

Man and bird locked eyes.

Bai Linlin couldn't help but chirp a few times.

*Holy crap, what a handsome young guy.*

chunks.chineseText:
面前的少年身形很高，约莫已经到了一米八，宽松的校服规矩地扣着，高领衣服上面是白皙的面庞。

额发其实是有些过长的，几乎盖住了眼睛，但却丝毫没有影响到优越的相貌。

鼻梁高挺，唇线平直。

垂着的眼睛，侧边还有颗血红的小痣。

“鸟？”

宋郁垂眸看着掌心的东西，没什么情绪起伏地说道。

也就在这时，门口的店老板冲了上来，张口就是：

“哎哎，我的鸟！”

活像是多心疼一样。

但其实是担心出了问题，待会交付卖不出去。

宋郁顺着声音看过去，店老板气喘吁吁的，手里的还拿着个竹竿。

“还你。”

这道声线很是冷淡。

白粼粼还没反应过来，就被往上一抛，他着急地又飞了起来，但或许是对这副新身躯不太适应，晃晃悠悠地就要掉地上。

梅开二度。

宋郁蹙眉，只好又接了一次。

掌心的蓝羽小鸟歪歪扭扭地要站起来，但在仰头看过去的一瞬间，眼珠子转了转。

鸟腿一弯，开始怪叫起来。

翅膀也意思意思地扑了两下。

“啾啾……啾啾……”

好不凄厉。

店老板一看，眉头都皱了，腿也瘸了？这鹦鹉一旦受伤，别说卖了，搞不好几天之后就会抑郁死了。

他几乎没多想，过去就开始倒打一耙，“哎哎，别走，你这把我鸟弄伤了怎么办？”

小巷里人来人往的。

倒是有人投过来目光，大多是看热闹的，毕竟这一个五大三粗的老板，拽着一个高中生。

很明显是在讹人。

宋郁仍然神色平静，直到对方说出了那句经典台词：

“你最低得给我……”

但话还没说完——

“我买了。”

空气一时有些尴尬，店老板搓了搓手，莫名觉得怪不好意思，这怎么没给他发挥空间？

但他还是灵活地去把店里的二维码拿了过来。

白粼粼金“鸡”独立，站在少年的肩头上，圆滚滚的鸟头歪了歪，看了下旁边的救命恩人。

这很明显是个高中生。

有钱赎他吗？

别不够。

白粼粼忧心忡忡地看少年的手机屏幕，对方修长的手指在屏幕上滑动着，切到了支付软件。

[指纹验证失败]

然后就是……

[4-5-3-2……]

宋郁总觉得视线感很强，侧头看过去，一人一鸟再度对视。

白粼粼有些尴尬，他就是看看密码，又不会做坏事。

宋郁面上没有什么表情，只是回头接着输了。

[4-5-3-2-8-6]

付过去了。

白粼粼一不小心就记住了，还不小心看到了误滑的另一个页面。

资产余额。

一共……嗯……七位数。

外面的虫子一下子就不好吃了。

就这样，鸟跟人回了家。

死心塌地。

-

路上。

白粼粼在人的肩头上东张西望的，心里感慨万分，不用走路原来这么爽。

他心想这也不错，不仅没死，反而重新投生了，还是宠物性质的鸟。

哈哈，死活也不当人了。

牛马要解放了！

“你自己能活么？”

白粼粼本来还在伸翅膀查看自己的羽毛的，闻言愣了下，这声音像是浸着冷气。

走这一段路的时候，古城墙的阴影覆了过来。

冷飕飕的。

“啾啾？”

少年似乎也只是自言自语，随后才很平静地补充，“你活不了。”

“算了。”

白粼粼总觉得这话怪怪的，但还来不及多观察几下，对方就停下了脚步。

到家了。

[我去！]

“啾啾！”

白粼粼震惊地看着这里，别墅，是别墅！

独栋，三层，小花园。

宋郁垂眸用指纹解锁栅栏，顺着青石台阶往前走，打开了玄关那里的门。

这里是南城，在古建筑旁边的别墅区，不是单纯的有钱就可以住进来的。

房子内部开着恒温空调，在四月多的时候不冷不热，里面的家居、岛台……鲜花……

每一处都相当温馨。

不过却没有什么居住的痕迹，反倒像是影视剧里的取景地。

[好好好好好！]

“啾啾啾啾啾！”

鸟很满意，鸟很激动，鸟要大鹏展翅。

白粼粼美美地在这房子里飞了一圈。

然后顺利降落至人的肩头。

[怎么样，飞得不错吧？]

“啾啾啾，啾啾啾啾啾？”

但面前的少年只是微微侧了下头，黑色的瞳孔里倒映着一只羽毛丰盈的小鸟。

宋郁语气很是平直：

“你不是腿瘸了么？”
chunks.englishText:
The young man standing before him was quite tall, easily reaching around one meter eighty. His loose school uniform was neatly buttoned, and above the high collar was a fair, delicate face.

His bangs were actually a bit too long, almost obscuring his eyes, yet doing nothing to diminish his superior looks.

A high-bridged nose with a straight, even lip line.

His lowered gaze revealed a tiny, blood-red mole resting near the corner of his eye.

"A bird?"

Song Yu lowered his gaze to look at the object in his palm, speaking with an utter lack of emotional fluctuation.

Right at that moment, the shop owner rushed out from the doorway, opening with:

"Hey, hey! My bird!"

He looked as though his heart was breaking.

In truth, he was merely worried something had gone wrong and he wouldn't be able to sell it later.

Song Yu followed the voice, looking over to see the shop owner panting heavily, still clutching a bamboo pole in his hand.

"Return it."

His tone of voice was exceptionally cold.

Before Bailinlin could even react, he was tossed upward into the air. Panic-stricken, he hastily tried to fly again, but perhaps still unaccustomed to this new body, he wobbled precariously as if about to plummet straight to the ground.

The tragedy repeated itself.

Song Yu frowned, and with no other choice, had to catch him a second time.

The little blue-feathered bird in his palm wobbled as it tried to stand, but the moment it raised its head to look up, its eyes rolled.

Its bird legs buckled, and it began to wail strangely.

Its wings also gave a token flutter.

*"Chirp-chirp... Chirp-chirp..."*

Utterly miserable.

Upon seeing this, the shop owner’s brow furrowed deeply. Was its leg broken, too? Once a parrot got injured, forget about selling it; for all he knew, it might die of depression in a few days.

Without a second thought, he lunged forward and turned the tables, accusing, "Hey, hey, don't you go anywhere! What am I supposed to do now that you've hurt my bird?"

The alleyway was filled with a steady stream of passersby.

Quite a few people cast glances over, mostly just rubbernecking. After all, here was a burly, rough-hewn shop owner grabbing a high school student by the collar.

It was blatantly extortion.

Song Yu maintained his calm expression until the other party uttered that classic line:

"At the very least, you have to give me..."

Before the words could even finish—

"I'll buy it."

The air turned somewhat awkward for a moment. The shop owner rubbed his hands together, feeling inexplicably embarrassed. How come he wasn't even given room to play his hand?

Still, he nimble-fingeredly fished out the shop's QR code.

Bailinlin stood unsteadily on one leg like a golden chicken atop the youth's shoulder, his round bird head tilting as he sized up his savior.

This was clearly just a high school student.

Did he even have enough money to ransom him?

I hope it's not short.

Bailinlin watched anxiously as the youth's slender fingers swiped across the screen, switching over to the payment app.

*[Fingerprint verification failed]*

And then…

*[4-5-3-2...]*

Song Yu instinctively felt a strong sense of being watched. He turned his head sideways, and man and bird locked eyes once more.

Bailinlin felt slightly awkward; he was just looking at the passcode, it wasn't like he was up to no good.

Song Yu wore no expression on his face as he simply turned back and continued inputting.

*[4-5-3-2-8-6]*

Payment successful.

Bailinlin accidentally memorized it, and accidentally caught a glimpse of another page he'd swiped to by mistake.

Account balance.

A total of... well... seven figures.

The bugs outside suddenly didn't look so appetizing anymore.

Just like that, the bird followed the human home.

Hook, line, and sinker.

-

Along the way.

Bailinlin looked around in wonder from atop the human's shoulder, feeling deeply emotional—not having to walk was simply amazing.

He thought to himself that this wasn't bad at all. Not only did he not die, but he'd been reincarnated into a new life as a pet bird.

Haha, who would ever want to be human again?

The beasts of burden are finally liberated!

"Can you survive on your own?"

Bailinlin was still busy stretching his wings to inspect his feathers when he froze at those words. The voice sounded as though it had been dipped in frost.

As they walked this stretch, the shadow of the ancient city wall fell over them.

It felt chilly.

*"Chirp?"*

The youth seemed to only be talking to himself, before adding very calmly, "You won't survive."

"Whatever."

Bailinlin always felt those words were a bit strange, but before he could observe any further, the other party came to a halt.

They had arrived home.

*[Holy crap!]*

*"Chirp!"*

Bailinlin stared in utter shock at the sight before him—a villa, it was a villa!

A detached, three-story house with a small garden.

Song Yu lowered his gaze to unlock the fence with his fingerprint, walked forward along the bluestone steps, and opened the door at the entryway.

This was Nancheng, a villa district nestled right beside ancient architecture. It wasn't a place you could move into simply by having money.

The interior of the house was kept at a constant temperature by air conditioning, leaving it neither cold nor warm in early April. The furniture inside, the kitchen island, the fresh flowers...

Every single detail was exceptionally cozy.

Yet, there were virtually no signs of habitation, making it look more like a film set from a TV drama.

*[Yes! Yes! Yes! Yes! Yes!]*

*"Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp!"*

The bird was satisfied; the bird was ecstatic; the bird was ready to spread its wings and soar.

Bailinlin joyfully took a flight around the house.

And then successfully landed back on the human's shoulder.

*[How was that? I fly pretty well, right?]*

*"Chirp chirp chirp, chirp chirp chirp chirp?"*

Yet the young man in front of him merely tilted his head slightly, his dark pupils reflecting a plump, fully-feathered little bird.

Song Yu spoke in a very flat tone:

"Didn't you say your leg was broken?"

chunks.chineseText:
第2章

空气有一瞬间的凝固。

宋郁垂着眼皮，看着肩头的小鸟，眉宇淡然。

白粼粼短暂思考了几秒，非常从善如流地鸟躯一歪。

啪唧摔倒了。

很拙劣的演技。

但就在这时，少年又恰如其分地开口：

“噢，鸟类腿部受伤好像不太影响飞行。”

对方的视线始终没有移动过。

“……”

白粼粼汗流浃背，心说不至于吧？这才过去不到一个小时，福尔摩斯探案也没这么快的。

人，你冒昧了。

一秒，两秒……

“我果然是病了，居然觉得一只鸟在我面前演戏。”

宋郁似乎是一下子抽离了出来，眉毛微微蹙着，自言自语道。

他抬手把肩头的小鸟拿了下来，面色有些冷。

但就在准备把这只活物放到玄关柜子上的时候。

停顿了下。

掌心的小鸟脑袋圆圆，两颊是蓬松的蓝羽，黑松石一样的眼睛很是亮，在歪头看他。

视线倘若再往下。

便可以看到漂亮的尾羽。

宋郁面色平静，但脑海成像：

bingo！

——蓝色雪顶甜筒。

但他脸色没有任何变化，只是把手中的小鸟放到了旁边，低头把校服给脱了。

白粼粼在一旁梳理了下自己的羽毛，心里还有些咯噔，反省了一下。

他毕竟现在是只鸟了。

不能做一些有违身份的事。

咳咳。

-

一楼的空间还是很大的。

白粼粼因为方才飞了一圈觉得实在过于高调，于是决定在地面行动。

人在前面走。

鸟在后面左右摇晃地往前蹦跶，时不时地四处看看。

这里毕竟是新家。

不过在经过岛台的时候，鸟腿停下了。

白粼粼闻到了非常浓郁的香气，他仰头一看，果然有个类似于食物保温的罩子。

几乎没有什么犹豫。

扑棱翅膀飞了上去。

白粼粼站在罩子上，低头一看，是一碗非常丰盛的牛肉面，色香味俱全，关键肉很大块。

！！

鸟非常着急。

他在玻璃罩子上站着，低头试图叨开那个罩子，但是喙实在是太小了，没有什么着力点。

完全就不如人手。

撬也撬不开。

白粼粼站在岛台上，自己和自己生闷气。

他是下班被创死了，还是没吃晚饭的那种！

啊！

与此同时。

宋郁上了楼，回到了自己卧室，抬手把衣服脱了，少年的躯体是精瘦的。

像是雏鹰，带着力量感。

他弯腰换了一件T恤，起身去抽屉里拿出来一瓶药。

倒在掌心，仰头吞服。

床头柜那里的水杯被拿了起来，大约一两秒后，被放回原地。

杯中水面晃动了下。

宋郁面色疲惫，弯腰拿过手机看了下，像是切了个页面，随后扔到了枕头边。

自己则是仰躺在了床上。

药物副作用会带来明显的困乏，视野也会变得不清晰，物体扭曲变形，仿佛张牙舞爪。

床头手机屏幕还在亮着。

——XXX鹦鹉滋养丸&种子粮。

——实付：689元。

——预计13：24送达。

宋郁意识浮浮沉沉，有些不太清醒，手背盖住了眼睛，有些隐隐的头晕。

水杯里的波纹还没有彻底平静，透过去可以看到那张优越的面庞，一点点地散开。

就在这时。

“叽嘎——叽嘎——”

“咚咚咚。”

“刺啦——”

后面声音制造者像是破防了一样，动静越来越大，从一开始的细细簌簌变成纯噪音。

宋郁盖在额头上的手指动了下，他的指腹有工笔刀划过的痕迹，不明显，但很深。

黑沉沉的梦被戳破了。

床上的人似乎有些怔然，他从未听过这么难听的声音，撑着手臂起来了。

走向门口，开门。

俯身蹲下。

宋郁的面容偏冷，瞳孔里更是没有光，但是此刻却莫名像是一面镜子。

倒映出来一个板板正正的小鸟。

“……”

白粼粼硬着头皮往上看，实在是没有办法，他没有办法弄开那个保温罩。

人吃，鸟才有机会吃。

“啾啾。”

[你好。]

宋郁无法确认自己现在的情绪，他只是觉得有点麻烦，抬手伸了过去，原本是想要拿起来的。

但是小鸟从善如流地站了上去，全然把手指当成了栖杆。

白粼粼本来以为搭上便车了，结果毫无动静，只能仰着鸟头看过去。

哎，这小孩长得实属好看。

皮肤白皙，额发垂着，睫毛也是根根分明，完全就是那种什么……国外男团成员，嗯对对！

白粼粼不由得也想起来自己，他满打满算也就工作了两年，原本在学校那也是风华正茂的。

还上过校草排行榜呢。

可惜过眼云烟。

“……”

鸟已经缅怀人生完了，怎么人还不站起来？

宋郁蹙了蹙眉，他其实觉得很奇怪的感觉，爪子包裹住手指，有软软的羽毛拂过皮肤。

很……很痒。

“啾啾啾？”

一道鸟叫声传来，让宋郁回了回神，看过去：

“你饿了？”

他的精神好了一些，意外地也没有被打扰的烦闷，索性问了问。

但问完又觉得自己有病。

面前的仅仅是一只不会学舌的鹦鹉，是不会回应——

宋郁刚准备起身，就看到手指上的小鸟点了点头。

或许是画面感太强。

少年又愣了一会。

白粼粼始终没有“起驾”，觉得很是奇怪，又仰着鸟头去看，顺带“啾啾”了几声。

催促了一下。

或许是因为角度的问题，肉色的短喙张开就可以露出来小舌头，一顶一顶的。

宋郁或许是因为刚吃过药，还有些不太清醒，他分明知道站在自己手上的是一只蓝羽和尚鹦鹉。

但脑子里全是一群短腿、黄毛……

“小鸡。”

几乎没有任何犹豫，不自觉就说出口了。

白粼粼震惊，气得毛都炸了炸，开始哐哐叫：

“啾啾啾啾，啾啾啾啾啾啾！”

[你才是鸡！你全家是小鸡！]

宋郁似乎是没有反应过来，劈头盖脸一顿“啾啾”，也没听懂什么意思。

只能判断是饿了。

他起身，端着手，往楼下走了。

-

白粼粼站在对方手上环视领地，觉得这房子真是不错。

人生糟糕，但鸟生圆满！

他蹦跶了两下，回头看了下少年，顿时又不生对方说自己“小鸡”的气了。

被物质蛊惑了鸟眼。

他伸了伸翅膀，飞到了“人”的肩头，很是宽宏大量。

宋郁侧头看了下，正好和鸟对视，说不上来什么情绪。

是觉得新奇么？

好像又不是。

他没有养过任何动物。

“啾啾啾？”

和尚鹦鹉本身具有很多优点，亲人，互动性高，但与此相对的……

就是吵。

以往空荡荡的别墅里，回荡着连续不断的“啾啾啾”。

宋郁只能判断这是饿了，因为在经过餐桌的时候，小鸟叫得尤为起劲。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 2 (Part 1)

For a brief moment, the air seemed to freeze.

Song Yu lowered his eyelids, gazing at the little bird perched on his shoulder, his expression utterly serene.

Bai Linlin pondered for a few seconds before sagely deciding to go with the flow: his tiny avian body reeled to the side...

*Plop.* 

He collapsed.

It was atrocious acting.

Yet right at that moment, the youth spoke up with impeccable timing:

"Ah. An injured leg doesn't seem to affect a bird's ability to fly."

His gaze hadn't shifted in the slightest.

"..."

Bai Linlin broke into a cold sweat, screaming inwardly. *Is this really necessary? It hasn't even been an hour! Even Sherlock Holmes wouldn't solve a case this fast!*

*Kid, you're stepping way out of line.*

One second, two seconds...

"I really must be sick, actually thinking a bird is performing for me."

Song Yu seemed to snap out of it all at once, his brows knitting slightly as he muttered to himself.

He raised his hand and plucked the little creature off his shoulder, his face somewhat cold.

However, just as he was about to set the living thing down on the hallway cabinet...

He paused.

In his palm, the little bird possessed a perfectly round head, fluffy blue feathers on its cheeks, and eyes as bright as polished black onyx, tilting its head to look up at him.

And if one shifted their gaze further down...

One could see its gorgeous tail feathers.

Song Yu's face remained placid, but an image mental render flashed in his mind:

*Bingo!*

—A blue snow-cap ice cream cone.

Yet, his expression didn't change at all. He simply set the bird aside, lowered his head, and unzipped his school uniform jacket to take it off.

Beside him, Bai Linlin preened his feathers, feeling a slight twinge of anxiety as he engaged in some self-reflection.

After all, he was a bird now.

He couldn't go around doing things that defied his current identity.

*Ahem.*

-

The space on the first floor was quite vast.

Because flying around earlier felt far too flashy, Bai Linlin decided to stick to ground travel.

The human walked ahead.

The bird waddled behind, swaying left and right as it hopped forward, casting curious glances around every now and then.

This was his new home, after all.

However, when passing by the kitchen island, the bird's legs came to a sudden halt.

Bai Linlin caught a whiff of an exceedingly rich, mouthwatering aroma. Looking up, he saw what appeared to be a glass food cover meant for keeping meals warm.

Without a moment's hesitation...

He flapped his wings and flew up.

Perched atop the glass cover, Bai Linlin looked down. Beneath it sat a sumptuous bowl of beef noodles—rich in color, fragrance, and taste, with tantalizingly large chunks of meat.

!!

The bird grew frantically impatient.

Standing on the glass dome, he leaned down and tried to peck the cover open, but his beak was far too small to get any leverage.

It couldn't compare to a human hand in the slightest.

Try as he might, he couldn't pry it open.

Bai Linlin stood on the kitchen island, stewing in his own frustration.

He had been struck dead by a vehicle right after getting off work—and on an empty stomach, no less!

*Argh!*

Meanwhile.

Song Yu had gone upstairs to his bedroom. Reaching up, he pulled off his clothes, revealing a lean, refined torso.

Like a young eagle, brimming with latent strength.

He bent down to change into a T-shirt, then stood up and pulled a bottle of medication from a drawer.

Pouring a few pills into his palm, he threw his head back and swallowed them raw.

He picked up the water glass on the nightstand, drank, and set it back in its original spot a second or two later.

The water inside rippled faintly.

Looking exhausted, Song Yu bent over to pick up his phone. He seemed to switch pages before tossing it onto the pillow.

Then, he collapsed flat onto the bed.

The medication's side effects brought a wave of heavy drowsiness, blurring his vision and causing surrounding objects to twist into grotesque, sprawling shadows.

On the nightstand, his phone screen was still lit.

—*XXX Parrot Nutritious Pellets & Seed Mix.*

—*Amount Paid: 689 RMB.*

—*Estimated Delivery: 13:24.*

Song Yu's consciousness drifted in a murky haze, far from lucid. He placed the back of his hand over his eyes, feeling a faint, dull headache.

The ripples in the water glass had yet to settle completely. Distorted through the glass, his striking face seemed to melt and scatter bit by bit.

Right at that moment.

"Ji-ga—Ji-ga—"

*Thump, thump, thump.*

*Screeech—*

The noise-maker downstairs seemed to have broken down completely; the sounds grew louder and louder, escalating from faint rustling into absolute racket.

Song Yu's fingers resting on his forehead twitched slightly. Traces of old cuts from an exacto knife were faintly visible on his pads—inconspicuous, but deep.

His dark, suffocating dream was shattered.

The person on the bed seemed slightly dazed. Having never heard such an ungodly racket before, he propped himself up by his arms.

He walked to the door and pulled it open.

Then, he squatted down.

Song Yu's features leaned cold, his pupils devoid of light, yet in this moment, they inexplicably resembled a mirror.

Reflected within them was a bird standing perfectly straight and proper.

"..."

Bai Linlin bit the bullet and looked up. He truly had no other choice—he simply couldn't get that thermal cover off.

Only when the human ate would the bird get a chance to feast.

"Chirp chirp."

[*Hello.*]

Song Yu couldn't make sense of his current emotions. He merely found the situation a bit troublesome. Reaching out a hand, he originally intended to pick the creature up.

However, the little bird casually stepped onto his finger, treating it entirely as a perch.

Bai Linlin had thought he was hitching a ride, but seeing no movement, he could only tilt his avian head up to look at the boy.

*Sigh, this kid really is ridiculously handsome.*

*Fair skin, soft bangs falling over his forehead, perfectly defined eyelashes... He looks just like one of those foreign boyband members! Yeah, exactly that!*

Bai Linlin couldn't help but reflect on his own past life. All told, he had only been in the workforce for two years, and back in college, he had been in the prime of his youth too.

He had even made it onto the campus heartthrob rankings!

Alas, all of it was now mere dust in the wind.

"..."

*The bird has finished reminiscing about its past life! Why hasn't the human stood up yet?*

Song Yu knit his brows. He actually felt a very strange sensation—tiny claws wrapping around his finger, with soft, silky feathers brushing against his skin.

It was... extremely ticklish.

"Chirp chirp chirp?"

A chorus of bird calls rang out, snapping Song Yu back to reality. He looked over:

"Are you hungry?"

His mind cleared up slightly. Surprised to find that he didn't feel his usual annoyance at being disturbed, he decided to just ask.

Though the moment the words left his mouth, he felt stupid.

The creature before him was merely an untrained parrot that couldn't even mimic speech; it couldn't possibly respond—

Just as Song Yu was about to stand up, he saw the little bird perched on his finger nod its head.

Perhaps because the image was so striking.

The youth froze once more.

Seeing that his "chariot" hadn't set off, Bai Linlin found it odd. He tilted his bird head up again, letting out a few "chirp chirps" to rush him along.

Perhaps owing to the angle, when its short, flesh-colored beak popped open, a tiny tongue could be seen bobbing up and down.

Song Yu, perhaps still somewhat hazy from the medication, clearly knew that standing on his hand was a blue-feathered Monk Parakeet.

Yet his mind was filled with images of short-legged, yellow-feathered...

"Little chick."

Without a moment's hesitation, the words slipped out of his mouth.

Bai Linlin was utterly stunned. Fuming so hard his feathers puffed into a round ball, he began to squawk frantically:

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp, chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp!"

[*You're the chick! Your whole family is little chicks!*]

Song Yu didn't seem to process what was happening. showered in a barrage of "chirp chirps," he couldn't understand a single word.

He could only deduce that it was starving.

Standing up, he held his hand steady and headed downstairs.

-

Standing atop the youth's hand, Bai Linlin surveyed his new domain, thinking this house was truly magnificent.

*Human life was a disaster, but bird life is perfection!*

He hopped twice, glanced back at the youth, and instantly forgave him for calling him a "little chick."

His avian eyes had been completely blinded by material luxury.

Stretching his wings, he flew onto the human's shoulder, acting exceedingly magnanimous.

Song Yu turned his head slightly, his gaze meeting the bird's directly, feeling an emotion he couldn't quite name.

Was it novelty?

It didn't seem like it.

He had never raised a pet before.

"Chirp chirp chirp?"

Monk Parakeets possessed many great qualities—they were affectionate and highly interactive. But on the flip side...

They were extremely noisy.

Through the usually desolate, empty villa, a continuous string of "chirps" echoed incessantly.

Song Yu could only assume it was hungry, because as they passed by the dining table, the bird's chirping reached an absolute crescendo.

chunks.chineseText:
他查了下手机，然后从厨房拿了个碟子，倒出来一点小米，打算应下急，给鸟端上了餐桌。

白粼粼：“……”

他吃这个？

鸟、鸟就吃这个？！

与此同时，桌子上的保温罩被掀开了，宋郁面色平静，似乎想起来自己也需要吃饭的事实。

准备动筷。

午饭是钟点工阿姨做的，对方一般掐着时间来的，不会露面。

这碗牛肉面鲜香四溢，没有任何可指摘之处。

但宋郁却在低头看过去的时候，不知道想起什么了，蹙了蹙眉，有些控制不住地面色泛白。

白粼粼也不敢违背人设，垂头丧气的，叨了口小米。

不好吃。

没有油炸鸡腿好吃，没有芝士汉堡好吃，没有脆脆薯条好吃，没有火腿披萨好吃……

啊！！！

白粼粼忘记这个重大bug了，他是可以住大别墅，可以不上班，可以躺平。

可是不能吃肉，不能上网，这鸟生有什么意义！

他决绝地扭过了头，今天无论如何也要叨走一块牛肉。

白粼粼视死如归。

鸟蹦蹦哒哒，逐步靠近。

但就在这时——

椅子发出很刺耳的声音，那少年离开了餐桌，似乎是去了一楼的洗手间。

白粼粼吓了一跳，翅膀都扑棱了两下，但又觉得这是个好机会，因为对方压根还没吃。

他飞了飞，爪子堪堪站在碗沿上。

但刚悄咪咪地垂下鸟头，就听到了不远处洗手间的动静。

有干呕声，还有很大的水流声。

白粼粼扭头看了过去，还是有些担心的，毕竟他是芯子里还是个“大人”，尽管工作也就两年，但看到高中生，还是很怜爱的。

这怎么了？生病了？

他挥了挥翅膀，没再去看那几块肉，而是飞到了洗手间的门把手上。

进不去。

鸟有些沮丧。

和尚鹦鹉是中型鹦鹉不错，但长宽高也就保温杯的一半，体重也就90-140克，很小的一只。

白粼粼往下踹了踹门把手，纹丝不动。

他后知后觉一件事，这个别墅确实很豪华，很漂亮，但是却没有什么人。

这少年父母呢？

鸟陷入了思考。

也就在这时，门被打开了，白粼粼没反应过来，只能一顿扑棱。

一双冰凉的手再次接住了他。

宋郁面容惨白、眼尾猩红，发梢甚至还沾了水，显得尤为黑。

他着实看起来不太“阳光”，只是低头看着掌心的鸟。

面无表情的。

轻声问：

“你找我？”

白粼粼呆呆的，也忘记了点头。

宋郁的声音的确是偏向于少年感，但却没有那种透彻的味道，像是某种石子落入深潭。

动听，但总会引起阵阵寒气。

“好乖。”

白粼粼鸟脸一红，什么东西，他只是过来看看他，现在小孩怎么说话没轻没重的。

宋郁其实是有些下三白的，但垂着眼皮看人，又不太明显，反倒是给人一种虚假的“亲和感”。

他走到了岛台那里，那碗面的味道依然很重，但他没有再反胃。

只是平摊着手，垂眸看着蓝色小鸟跳下来。

“啾啾啾？”

[怎么了？]

白粼粼仰着头，说实话不太了解对方要做什么，这纯粹就是个高中生。

生病要看医生的。

厌食？

正当鸟头脑风暴的时候，有碟子挪动的声音，白粼粼回了回神。

低头一看。

生小米。

“……”

白粼粼不为所动，他是真的不爱吃，于是超绝不经意地去梳理自己的羽毛了。

也就在这时。

“厌食？”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 2 (Part 2)

He checked his phone, went into the kitchen to grab a small saucer, and poured out a bit of millet. Intending to use it as a makeshift fix, he carried it over to the dining table for the bird.

Bai Linlin: "..."

*He's supposed to eat THIS?*

*A b-bird eats THIS?!*

At the same time, Song Yu lifted the thermal cover off the table. With an impassive expression, he seemed to remember the fact that he needed to eat as well.

He prepared to pick up his chopsticks.

Lunch had been prepared by the hourly maid, who usually timed her visits carefully to avoid making an appearance.

The bowl of beef noodles overflowed with a rich, savory aroma, entirely flawless in every aspect.

Yet, as Song Yu lowered his head to look at it, something seemed to cross his mind. His brows furrowed tightly, and his face turned uncontrollably pale.

Not daring to break character, Bai Linlin hung his head dejectedly and took a peck at the raw millet.

Disgusting.

Not as delicious as fried chicken legs, not as delicious as cheeseburgers, not as delicious as crispy French fries, not as delicious as ham pizza...

*AHHH!!!*

Bai Linlin had forgotten a major flaw in his situation! Sure, he got to live in a grand villa, didn't have to work, and could just lie back and relax...

But if he couldn't eat meat or surf the internet, what was the point of living as a bird?!

He turned his head away with utter resolve. Today, come hell or high water, he was going to snatch a piece of that beef.

Bai Linlin had a look of tragic solemnity, ready to meet his doom.

The bird hopped along, step by step, gradually drawing closer.

Just then—

The chair produced a harsh, grating screech as the youth abruptly abandoned the dining table, seemingly heading toward the first-floor bathroom.

Bai Linlin jumped in surprise, his wings flapping wildly. However, realizing this was a golden opportunity since the boy hadn't touched his food yet, he took flight and landed right on the edge of the bowl.

Yet just as he covertly lowered his avian head, he caught the sound of commotion coming from the nearby bathroom.

There were sounds of dry-heaving, followed by the roar of running water.

Bai Linlin turned his head to look, feeling a pang of worry. Deep down, he was still an "adult." Though he had only been working for two years, he couldn't help but feel a sense of pity for a high school student.

*What's wrong with him? Is he sick?*

Flapping his wings, he paid no more mind to those chunks of beef, flying over to perch on the bathroom door handle instead.

He couldn't get in.

The bird felt a wave of frustration.

Monk Parakeets were indeed medium-sized parrots, but in height and width, he was only half the size of a thermos cup, weighing a mere 90 to 140 grams. He was tiny.

Bai Linlin kicked down on the door handle with his claws, but it didn't budge an inch.

Then, a sudden realization hit him: this villa was indeed luxurious and beautiful, but it was eerily devoid of people.

*Where are this kid's parents?*

The bird fell into deep thought.

Right at that moment, the door swung open. Caught off guard, Bai Linlin could only flap his wings frantically.

A pair of icy hands caught him once again.

Song Yu's face was deathly pale, the corners of his eyes crimson, and the tips of his dark hair clung to his forehead, damp with water.

He truly looked anything but "bright and cheerful." He merely stared down at the bird in his palm.

Expressionless.

He asked softly:

"Were you looking for me?"

Bai Linlin stared blankly, even forgetting to nod.

Song Yu's voice did possess a youthful quality, yet it lacked any sense of warmth or clarity. It sounded like stones dropping into a deep, dark pool—melodic, but always summoning a draft of chill.

"So good."

Bai Linlin's bird face flushed red. *What on earth? I just came over to check on you! Kids these days really don't filter their words!*

Song Yu actually had slightly sharp, sanpaku eyes, but when he lowered his eyelids, it wasn't very noticeable, instead giving off a deceptive air of "approachability."

He walked over to the kitchen island. Though the aroma of the noodles remained strong, he no longer felt like gagging.

He simply flattened his palm, lowering his eyes as he watched the blue bird hop down.

"Chirp chirp chirp?"

[*What's wrong?*]

Tilting his head up, Bai Linlin honestly had no idea what the boy was planning. He was just a high school kid, after all.

*If you're sick, you need to see a doctor.*

*Anorexia?*

Just as the bird was brainstorming, the sound of a dish sliding echoed. Bai Linlin snapped back to his senses.

He looked down.

Raw millet.

"..."

Bai Linlin remained unmoved. He genuinely hated the stuff, so he nonchalantly began preening his feathers, pretending not to notice.

Right then.

"Anorexia?"

chunks.chineseText:
第3章

小米其实是属于鹦鹉喜好的食物之一，但由于营养不够全面，通常是不作为主食的。

已经相当于“零食”了。

白粼粼没办法，硬着头皮叨了一口，硬邦邦的，这到底有什么好吃的。

但似乎是因为他这个动作。

周遭沉郁的氛围消散了些。

“待会你的食物就到了。”

“不要着急。”

这道声音显得很温和，宋郁垂眸看了一眼，之后起身把桌上未动的饭菜收走了。

白粼粼着急地在桌面上蹦跶了几下，觉得这简直是暴殄天物。

也就在这时，门铃响了。

宋郁从厨房走出来，垂眸看了下手机，似乎是在看订购的鸟粮页面，抬手打开了门。

白粼粼虽然慢了一些，但还是在后面飞了过来。

……

门外站的是个二十多岁的青年，鼻梁上架着一副眼镜，文质彬彬的，看着有种“老学究”的味道。

在这人身后，有一个推车，上面放着高高低低一堆鸟粮袋子，周遭还有陪同的几名物业人员。

阵仗有些过于大了。

“这些都是？”

宋郁嗓音有些偏冷，略微不解，但还没有得到回答，耳廓有一阵风。

小鸟收了收翅膀，很是顺利降落，爪子在人肩膀上站得稳稳当当。

“小宋，这就是你买的鸟啊？”

齐思扬弯腰去看了看，居然是最近炒得很热的和尚鹦鹉，这个品种价格从两千到五千不等。

这祖宗真要养鸟？

稀奇。

不过他还有正事要说，微微抬了下眉，环着手臂道：

“老师特地嘱咐我全给带回来，顺带问问到底怎么回事。”

“爱羽平台在维修中的，那些价格特地调高了，你怎么还下单了？ ”

“还有，你数量也不看，你知道你买了一百斤鸟粮么？”

白粼粼站在宋郁肩头，本来威风凛凛，但看着推车上的东西，一阵沉默，鸟爪往旁边挪了下，试图飞回去。

没有什么热闹可看。

但就在鸟头下压，尾羽上翘的时候——

“噢，没事。”

宋郁一边平和地交谈，一边抬手扣住了鸟，修长的指缝里有蓬松的羽毛穿过，小鸡的喙滑滑的，似乎是叨了一口，但没太用力。

少年从容地补了句：

“代我向陈爷爷问好。”

陈开鹤是南市一所农业大学的客座教授，和宋郁的爷爷是上过战场的关系，说是“亲兄弟”都不为过了，他本人没有婚配，对于老友膝下这么个小辈，自然是疼爱的。

而齐思扬正是陈老先生的学生，博二了，偶尔也会来锦园这边替老师送点东西，一来二去也认识这位含着金汤匙的少爷了。

“这你放心，老师只是最近有些忙，还在国外。”

说到这里，青年语气一顿，迟疑地补了句：

“宋老先生一定会平安的。”

白粼粼隐约听出来点八卦的意思，仰着鸟头，爪子垂着，把喙往上伸了伸。

全神贯注。

他现在连这饲主的名字都不知道的，看来是姓宋？

那是宋……宋什么？

“运进去吧。”齐思扬回头吩咐了下师傅，这些如同小山的鸟粮就进了家门，堆在玄关。

白粼粼：“……”

他真不中了。

一个大好青年，正是吃垃圾食品的时候，现在给他整上粗粮了。

一夜回到解放前。

-

宋郁下午需要上课，他情绪照旧还是消沉，但还是又花了些时间，去看鸟吃饭。

鸟不吃。

僵持。

白粼粼又没觉得多饿，他是真的不愿意吃生的东西，粮食也不行，又没味道。

只是在岛台上梳理羽毛，故作看不见盘子里的东西。

“为什么不吃。”

少年的语气没有什么起伏，很轻，眼皮垂着。

气氛其实不是很好。

但鸟没有察觉到。

白粼粼是在尾随到玄关的时候，才发现对方要走了，高中生是有课的。

好惨。

宋郁面色暗沉，眼尾的痣在背光下若隐若现的，他转身看过来，最后附身半蹲道：

“这样，下午要吃饭。”

“……”

“啾啾？”

门关上了，偌大的别墅里只剩下鸟一个。

白粼粼在一楼转了转，最终还是绕到了厨房，仿佛是下定了决心。

冰箱的门没有关紧，有一道缝隙，里面有钟点工阿姨的备品，卤好的肉类、新鲜的水果，还有一些带有包装的饮料。

都摆放得很齐整。

里面有隔间，还有保鲜膜。

此刻，肉色的小短喙伸了进来，非常努力地去撬冰箱门。

一下。

两下。

“啾——”

白粼粼爪子都要往下滑了，但好在是弄开了，他扑棱翅膀飞了上去，感受到了冰箱里的阵阵寒气。

不过这都不要紧。

鸟一下子叨开了保鲜膜，品鉴了一下卤牛肉，简直美味！

白粼粼也不是对自己不负责，他只是考虑了下，一辈子吃鸟粮、没wifi，还是免费活一天？

他本来就死过了。

从店老板那里逃出来，是事关鸟体尊严，就算不碰瓷这少年，他也还是会捯饬点垃圾食品的。

但鸟可以吃垃圾食品吗？

恐怕不行。

白粼粼扑棱了下翅膀，飞回到了厨房台面上，闭上了鸟眼。

等死。

脑子里开始胡思乱想。

其实转生成国宝也不行，熊猫天天啃竹子；转生成猫猫狗狗也不行，尽管科技发达，但好像不能吃麻辣烫吧？

不能吃咸香麻辣，那有什么意思？

白粼粼羽毛蓬松，鸟眼很是安详地闭着，愈发觉得自己想的没错。

噢，对了。

他的某博、某书、某音辱骂领导的帖子好像没删，会不会被查；前几天那个塌方明星的瓜还没吃明白，哎，到底是吞了几个亿；公司美术组组长私底下约炮的聊天记录他还没看完。

哎呀！

白粼粼的毛越来越炸，最后窝在大理石板上，成了个球。

真是不爽！

不过。

他睁开眼睛，发现一切如常，没有死，咂巴匝巴喙，还是香香的。

白粼粼低头看了看自己的身体，很遗憾，连脚都看不到，只有蓬松的羽毛。

“啾啾?”

[奇怪？]

他想了想——

那岂不是还可以再炫一块？

白粼粼再度飞了过去，熟练地叼了一块肉，不大不小，刚好够吃。

炫完又等了下。

一秒，两秒。

“咕咕……”

白粼粼觉得有些饿，但他也反应过来有点奇怪，低头看了看自己的身躯。

自己体型不大的。

两块肉……还不够？

不管了！

厨房里传来细细簌簌的声音。

-

三小时后。

冰箱里的保鲜膜基本都被叨开了，一律吃了个遍，鸟很满意。

白粼粼觉得自己可能天赋异禀，他又好起来了，然后开始在别墅里转。

门起初是很难打开的。

但或许是因为吃了东西，有力气了，白粼粼还真就打开了一扇门。

就是那少年的卧室。

鸟探头探脑的，有些好奇。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 3 (Part 1)

Millet was actually one of a parrot's favorite foods, but due to its incomplete nutritional profile, it was rarely used as a staple diet.

It was essentially a "treat."

Having no choice, Bai Linlin bit the bullet and took a peck. Hard as a rock—what was so good about this anyway?

Yet, seemingly due to his action...

The somber, oppressive atmosphere surrounding them thinned slightly.

"Your food will be here shortly."

"Don't be impatient."

The voice sounded quite gentle. Song Yu cast a downcast glance at him, then stood up to clear away the untouched food on the table.

Bai Linlin hopped anxiously across the tabletop, thinking this was an absolute waste of fine food.

Just then, the doorbell rang.

Song Yu walked out of the kitchen, checked his phone—seemingly reviewing the bird food order page—and reached out to open the door.

Though a bit slower, Bai Linlin flapped his wings and flew over behind him.

...

Standing outside was a young man in his twenties, wearing a pair of glasses on the bridge of his nose. He looked refined and scholarly, carrying the air of a veteran academic.

Behind him was a handcart stacked high with bags of bird food of various sizes, accompanied by several property management staff members.

The sheer scale of it was a bit excessive.

"All of these are mine?"

Song Yu's voice leaned cold, tinged with slight confusion. But before he received an answer, a gust of wind brushed past his ear.

The little bird folded its wings and executed a flawless landing, its claws clamping firmly onto his shoulder.

"Little Song, is this the bird you bought?"

Qi Siyang bent down to take a look. It was actually a Monk Parakeet, a species that had been trending recently, with prices ranging anywhere from two thousand to five thousand RMB.

*Was this young master really going to raise a bird?*

*Now that's a rarity.*

However, he still had proper business to attend to. Raising an eyebrow slightly, he folded his arms and said:

"Professor specifically instructed me to bring all of this over, and to ask what on earth happened."

"The Aiyu platform was undergoing maintenance, so those prices were artificially jacked up. Why did you still place the order?"

"And you didn't even check the quantity! Do you have any idea that you bought a hundred jin of bird food?"

Standing on Song Yu's shoulder, Bai Linlin had originally felt quite majestic, but staring at the mountain of supplies on the cart, he fell into a stunned silence. His claws shifted to the side as he contemplated flying back inside.

There was clearly no fun drama to watch here.

Yet, just as the bird lowered its head and raised its tail feathers to take off—

"Oh, it's fine."

While conversing calmly, Song Yu reached up and held the bird gently in place. Soft, fluffy feathers slipped between his long fingers; the chick's beak was slick, pecking at him lightly, though without much force.

The youth smoothly added:

"Please send my regards to Grandpa Chen."

Chen Kaihe was a visiting professor at an agricultural university in Nanshi, an old comrade-in-arms of Song Yu's grandfather from their days on the battlefield. Calling them "blood brothers" wouldn't be an exaggeration. Having never married, he naturally doted on this junior descendant of his old friend.

As for Qi Siyang, he was Professor Chen's second-year PhD student. He occasionally came over to the Jinyuan estate to deliver things for his mentor, and over time, he had gotten to know this young master born with a silver spoon in his mouth.

"You can rest assured on that front. Professor is just a bit busy lately and still abroad."

At this point, the young man paused, adding with a hint of hesitation:

"Old Master Song will definitely recover safely."

Bai Linlin caught a subtle whiff of gossip. Tilting his bird head, claws hanging loose, he stretched his beak upward.

He was all ears.

He didn't even know his owner's full name yet. It seemed his surname was Song?

So... Song what?

"Bring them inside," Qi Siyang turned around and instructed the workers. The small mountain of bird food was brought into the house, stacked high in the entryway foyer.

Bai Linlin: "..."

*He really couldn't take this anymore.*

*A fine young man in the prime of his life, an age meant for indulging in junk food, and now he was being forced onto a coarse-grain diet.*

*Straight back to the dark ages overnight.*

-

Song Yu had classes to attend in the afternoon. Though his mood remained subdued, he still took some time to watch the bird eat.

The bird refused.

A total stalemate.

Bai Linlin didn't even feel that hungry. He genuinely refused to eat raw food—grain was no exception, especially when it tasted like nothing.

He simply stood on the kitchen island preening his feathers, pointedly ignoring the contents of the dish.

"Why aren't you eating?"

The youth's voice carried no inflection, extremely soft, his eyelids drooping.

The atmosphere was rather heavy.

Yet the bird remained blissfully unaware.

It was only when Bai Linlin followed him all the way to the entryway that he realized the boy was leaving. High schoolers had classes, after all.

How tragic.

Song Yu's face was dark. The mole at the corner of his eye flickered in and out of the shadows. He turned back, finally crouching down halfway:

"Be good. Eat your food this afternoon."

"..."

"Chirp chirp?"

The door clicked shut, leaving the bird all alone in the vast villa.

Bai Linlin ambled around the first floor, eventually winding his way back to the kitchen, looking as if he had made up his mind.

The refrigerator door wasn't fully closed, leaving a sliver of a gap. Inside were supplies prepared by the hourly maid: braised meats, fresh fruit, and packaged beverages.

Everything was neatly arranged.

Inside were compartments wrapped in plastic film.

Right now, a short, flesh-colored beak poked inside, working tirelessly to pry the fridge door open.

Once.

Twice.

"Chirp—"

Bai Linlin's claws almost lost their grip, but luckily, he managed to wedge it open. Flapping his wings, he flew inside, immediately greeted by gusts of chilly air from the fridge.

None of that mattered, though.

The bird promptly pecked open the plastic wrap and took a taste of the braised beef. Absolute bliss!

Bai Linlin wasn't being irresponsible with his own life. He had simply weighed his options: a lifetime of bird food and no Wi-Fi, versus living one free, glorious day?

He had already died once anyway!

Escaping from that pet shop owner was a matter of avian dignity. Even if he hadn't glommed onto this youth, he still would have scavenged for some junk food regardless.

*So, can a bird eat human food?*

*Probably not.*

Bai Linlin fluttered his wings, flew back to the kitchen counter, and closed his eyes.

Awaiting death.

Random thoughts began to swirl in his mind.

*Honestly, being reincarnated as a national treasure wouldn't be great either—pandas munch on bamboo all day. Being reincarnated as a cat or dog isn't ideal either; despite advanced technology, they probably can't eat spicy hotpot, right?*

*If you can't eat savory, fragrant, spicy food, what's the point of living?*

Bai Linlin's feathers puffed up, his eyes closed in serene peace, feeling increasingly convinced that his logic was sound.

*Oh, right.*

*He hadn't deleted those draft posts on Weibo, Xiaohongshu, and Douyin where he badmouthed his boss—would he get investigated? And the celebrity scandal from a few days ago—he hadn't quite figured out if the guy embezzled hundreds of millions or what. Also, he hadn't finished reading the leaked chat logs of his company's art director secretly hooking up with people online!*

*Ah, damn it!*

Bai Linlin's feathers fluffed up more and more until he curled into a round, puffy ball on the marble counter.

*This is so frustrating!*

However.

He opened his eyes and found that everything was completely normal. He hadn't died. Smacking his beak a couple of times, he could still taste the savory lingering flavor.

Bai Linlin looked down at his body. Regrettably, he couldn't even see his own feet—just a fluff of feathers.

"Chirp chirp?"

[*Strange?*]

He pondered for a moment—

*Does that mean I can gobble down another piece?*

Bai Linlin flew over once more and adeptly snatched a piece of meat—not too big, not too small, just the right size to swallow.

After scarfing it down, he waited again.

One second, two seconds.

"Gurgle..."

Bai Linlin felt a bit hungry, but he also realized something was off. He looked down at his tiny frame.

He wasn't very big.

Two pieces of meat... and he still wasn't full?

*Whatever!*

Faint rustling noises echoed through the kitchen.

-

Three hours later.

Almost all the plastic wrap in the fridge had been pecked open. Everything had been sampled, leaving the bird thoroughly satisfied.

Bai Linlin felt that he might be extraordinarily gifted—he felt great again! He then began to wander around the villa.

The doors were initially difficult to open.

However, perhaps because he had eaten and regained his strength, Bai Linlin actually managed to nudge one open.

It was the youth's bedroom.

The bird poked its head in, brimmed with curiosity.

chunks.chineseText:
白粼粼的愿望还有一个，就是打下游戏，他还是不确定自己吃完肉之后还会不会死掉，尽管现在……鸟体安康。

卧室整个的格调是偏暗沉的。

深色木质家居占主色，有沙发，台灯，还有电脑桌，很空旷。

但光线不好，窗帘都是没有拉开的。

阴气森森的。

白粼粼飞到了桌子那里，不知道怎么回事，没有着急去研究怎么开机电脑。

反倒是被旁边的一个相框吸引住了。

那是一张全家福。

男人相貌堂堂，西服革履，看起来风流倜傥；女人则是身着白色礼裙，秀发垂在胸前，笑得很温婉。

中间是个男孩。

眉眼……白粼粼愣了下，这实在是不怪他反应不过来。

这照片上的小孩气质相当阳光，眼角都是往上的。

实在是和现实中的少年不沾边。

啧。

白粼粼在桌面上蹦跶了几下，很快就有了新发现，因为旁边就摆着一本教辅书。

他用喙叼起来一页纸。

垂眸看到了扉页的姓名。

【宋郁】

白粼粼蹙了蹙眉，只有一个单字么？那看起来很愁闷的样子。

谁给他取的？

不过自己的名字也很随便了。

白粼粼不自觉地怀念起小时候，当时在福利院学习，他就是不愿意写复杂的字，只乐意写“一二三四。”

甚至认认真真和老师说，自己以后叫“一一。”

后面当然是被批评教育了。

白粼粼不由得觉得乐，因为他的姓是自己取的，但“粼”是老师定下来的，就是因为他总嫌弃字的笔画多，反倒是最后被将了一军。

写的最多的就是“粼”了。

哎……

过往云烟。

鸟再次感怀，并愤愤不平那辆不踩刹车的运土车，仗着自己有保险是吧？

你用力地活着。

我死了！

不过也就在这时，白粼粼低头一看，这才震惊地发现自己把宋郁的教辅书封面给咬出来个齐齐的条。

每一个弧度，都是鸟嘴的印。

“……”

他着急了，低头去叼住那个纸条，放回去。

根本就不贴合！

完了。

-

白粼粼最后没办法了，把那本书用鸟腿往里踹了踹，叼着纸条环顾房间。

本来是想要藏起来的。

但不知道为什么，他脑子一抽，把那个彩色封皮纸条，插到自己尾羽上了。

“……”

鸟蹦跶了一下。

白粼粼转了转身体，灵机一动，用肉色的短喙又把纸条往里戳了戳。

蓝羽盖住了。

嘿嘿，这样就好了。

白粼粼觉得自己聪明绝顶，本来是想要去看看这旁边的电脑是什么型号的，他还剩下个打游戏的心愿。

但是就在这时，窗户外面传来些动静。

有密码锁的提示音。

宋郁回来了？

鸟一下子着急，扑棱翅膀逃离犯罪现场，爪子扣在门把手上，往外拉了拉。

砰——

关上了。

白粼粼有些意外，嚯，他力气居然还不小，是因为吃了肉吗？

自己还没死？

他有点隐隐约约的猜想，万一，万一……世界其他鹦鹉品种不变，只有我独自进化。

“小鸡。”

楼下传来一道少年音，平静，沉稳。

宋郁没有上晚课，他把外套放在了玄关，抬眸看着楼上。

别墅很大，水晶吊灯是贯穿一二楼的，因而从客厅往上看，是可以看到一只蓝羽小鸟站在门把手上的。

白粼粼愣了下，本来是想否认自己不是小鸡的，但是翅膀却先动了。

或许是彻底适应身体了。

他飞得很顺利，端端正正地站在了宋郁的肩头。

少年侧眸看了过去，修长的手指伸了过来。

圆滚滚的鸟头歪了歪，眼睛朝上看了看，试探地把爪子挪了过去，站好了。

白粼粼没有再装腿瘸了，反正早就被发现了，不过在对视的时候莫名有些不自在，于是歪头梳理了下羽毛。

但就在这时——

一根啃得错落有致的纸条在尾羽中冒了出来。

宋郁抬手抽了出来，看了一眼。

“……”

白粼粼本来还不知道，结果感觉尾羽被抽出来什么，仰头一看，鸟眼瞪得浑圆。

“啾啾啾啾……”

[还我还我。]

宋郁面色平静，把手往上抬了下，不过视线已经转移了，在看站在手指上的小鸟。

肉色短喙一张一合的，里面的小舌头犹如一个棒槌，往上顶。

“……”

白粼粼看到对方手抬高了，整个鸟都气到了，仗着自己个儿高是不是！

过分过分。

他也不知道怎么了，忘记了自己有翅膀了，在宋郁闷的手指上蹦跶了好几下。

结果差点重心不稳。

坠落——

宋郁抬手接住了，顺带把纸条还给了鸟，没说什么，只是朝岛台那里走了过去。

白粼粼叼到了自己的纸条，也给愣住了。

不是，他抢这个干什么？

已经被发现了的。

他不愿意承认自己被某种底层代码给硬控了。

“……”

白粼粼叼着也费劲，思来想去，还是又歪头插自己尾羽上了。

安心ing。

-

宋郁垂眸看着那个瓷盘，里面的鸟粮仍然是满满一盘，没有任何食用过的痕迹。

他拉开椅子，坐下，抬眸看向手指上的小鸟，很淡漠。

白粼粼正在扭头检查自己的尾羽，结果一回头，一下子对视了起来。

鸟吓了一跳，差点没往后一仰栽倒。

“我果然养不活你。”

宋郁的语调没有什么起伏，他已经查询过了鹦鹉厌食的原因，排除生理原因，就是情绪上的问题。

抑郁、焦虑……

对现状不满。

他的腕骨传来一阵阵的刺痛，手指也不由得轻颤了下，宋郁蹙了蹙眉，分明已经吃过药了。

少年本来是打算收回来手的。

但是鸟察觉到这个意图后，爪子紧紧地扣住了。

“……”

没办法，宋郁只能保持不动，用左手拿出来手机，联系了下齐思扬。

手机屏幕上的光闪了下，似乎是对面回了消息。

白粼粼还没太反应过来，他只是觉得自己应该是个进化过的鸟，完全没必要吃那些鸟粮的。

至于养不养得活……

白粼粼腹诽，这青少年怎么这么爱想东想西，他在宋郁的手上蹦跶了下，结果爪子意外勾到了对方的袖子，导致衣服往上堆叠了下。

手腕露了出来。

上面是一道道的刀痕。

鸟愣住了。

宋郁在垂眸发消息，没有发觉自己的袖子被勾丝了，不过就在他处理好事情后，抬眼看过来的瞬间。

白粼粼立刻用鸟爪又勾下去那块布料了，盖得严严实实的。

蓬松的脑袋圆圆的，鸟头一瞥，站姿尤为标准，倒真的像是八音盒上的发条鸟了。

“……”

宋郁本来是想说点什么，但又觉得自己真的是病了，居然会想着对一只鸟说话。

它又听不懂。

他保持着右手不动，看着蓝羽小鸟梳理羽毛，全然是把自己的手当成了栖杆。

直到手机传来嗡嗡的震动声。
chunks.englishText:
Bai Linlin had one more wish: to play a video game. He still wasn't entirely sure whether eating meat would kill him, even though... his avian body currently felt perfectly hale and hearty.

The master bedroom's aesthetic leaned toward dark and somber.

Dark wood furniture dominated the palette—a sofa, a desk lamp, and a computer desk stood in the vast, empty space. 

However, the lighting was dismal, as the curtains were drawn tight.

It felt chillingly gloomy.

Bai Linlin fluttered over to the desk. For some reason, instead of figuring out how to turn on the computer, his attention was immediately snagged by a framed photo beside it.

It was a family portrait.

The man was handsome and well-groomed, clad in a sharp suit that gave him a refined, dapper air. The woman wore a white formal gown, her hair falling softly over her chest, smiling with gentle grace.

In the middle stood a young boy.

His facial features... Bai Linlin froze. It really wasn't his fault for failing to make the connection right away.

The child in the photograph possessed a remarkably sunny disposition, the corners of his eyes crinkling upward with warmth.

He looked absolutely nothing like the youth in real life.

*Tsk.*

Bai Linlin hopped around on the desktop a few times and soon made a new discovery: a supplementary workbook was laying right beside the photo.

He used his beak to nip open a page.

Lowering his gaze, he saw the name written on the title page.

【Song Yu】

Bai Linlin knitted his tiny brows. *Just a single given name? Sounds rather melancholic. Who named him that?*

Then again, his own name had been picked pretty casually, too.

Bai Linlin couldn't help but reminisce about his childhood back at the orphanage. When learning to write, he had hated dealing with complex characters and only wanted to write "one, two, three, four." He had even earnestly told his teacher that he wanted to be called "Yi Yi" (One-One) from then on.

Naturally, he had received a stern lecturing for that.

Bai Linlin found it amused to look back on. He had chosen his own surname, but the character "Lin" had been assigned by the teacher. Precisely because he kept complaining about characters having too many strokes, the teacher had checked him into a corner. In the end, the word he had to write the most was "Lin."

*Ah...*

*All past dust and smoke.*

The bird sighed emotionally once more, inwardly cursing the dump truck driver who hadn't hit the brakes. *Relying on your insurance, were you?*

*You lived your life with all your might.*

*And I ended up dead!*

Right at that moment, however, Bai Linlin looked down—only to be horrified to find that he had bitten off a clean, serrated strip from the cover of Song Yu's workbook.

Every single curve bore the unmistakable imprint of a parrot's beak.

"..."

Panicking, he bent down to scoop up the strip of paper with his beak, trying to stick it back.

It didn't fit at all!

*I'm done for.*

-

Having no other choice, Bai Linlin used his bird legs to kick the book further inward. Then, holding the paper strip in his beak, he scanned the room.

He had originally intended to hide it somewhere.

Yet for reasons unknown, his brain suffered a sudden short circuit, and he shoved the colorful strip of paper straight into his own tail feathers.

"..."

The bird hopped once.

Bai Linlin swiveled his body, had a stroke of brilliance, and used his flesh-colored beak to poke the paper strip deeper inside.

The blue feathers covered it up nicely.

*Hehe, good to go.*

Bai Linlin thought he was a absolute genius. He was just about to check the specifications of the nearby computer to fulfill his final wish of playing a game when a noise echoed from outside the window.

It was the chime of the digital door lock.

Song Yu was back?

Panicking instantly, the bird flapped his wings to flee the scene of the crime. Hooking his claws around the door handle, he pulled outward.

*Bang—*

The door slammed shut.

Bai Linlin was somewhat surprised. *Whoa, my strength isn't small at all! Is it because I ate meat?*

*I'm really not dead yet?*

A faint theory flickered in his mind: *What if... what if other parrot species in the world remain unchanged, and I alone am evolving?*

"Little Chick."

A youth's voice floated up from downstairs—calm and steady.

Song Yu hadn't stayed for evening classes. He left his jacket at the entryway and looked up toward the second floor.

The villa was vast, with a crystal chandelier spanning between the first and second levels. Looking up from the living room, one could clearly see a small blue-feathered bird perched on the door handle.

Bai Linlin froze. He had intended to deny that he was a chick, but his wings moved before his mind could catch up.

Perhaps he had completely adapted to his new body.

He flew down smoothly and landed squarely on Song Yu's shoulder.

The youth glanced sideways, extending a long, slender finger.

The plump bird head tilted. Eyes looking upward, he tentatively shifted his claws over and stood firm.

Bai Linlin stopped pretending his leg was lame; after all, he'd already been found out anyway. Still, feeling oddly self-conscious under the youth's gaze, he tilted his head to preen his feathers.

Just then—

A neatly chewed paper strip poked out from among his tail feathers.

Song Yu reached up, pulled it out, and glanced at it.

"..."

Bai Linlin hadn't realized it at first. But feeling something being yanked from his tail feathers, he looked up, his bird eyes widening into perfectly round circles.

"Chirp chirp chirp chirp..."

*[Give it back, give it back!]*

With a calm expression, Song Yu raised his hand slightly higher, though his gaze had already shifted to observe the small bird standing on his finger.

The flesh-colored beak opened and closed rapidly, the tiny tongue inside bobbing up like a little mallet.

"..."

Seeing the youth raise his hand higher, Bai Linlin blew a fuse. *Taking advantage of your height, are you?!*

*Too much, absolutely too much!*

Without realizing why, he completely forgot he possessed wings and hopped frantically up and down on Song Yu's finger.

As a result, he nearly lost his center of gravity.

Plummeting—

Song Yu raised his hand to catch him, returning the paper strip to the bird in the process. Saying nothing, he simply walked toward the kitchen island.

Holding his paper strip in his beak, Bai Linlin was stunned.

Wait, why did he even snatch this back?

He'd already been caught red-handed!

He refused to admit that he was hard-coded by some low-level animal instinct.

"..."

Holding it in his beak was tiring. After careful consideration, Bai Linlin tilted his head and shoved it back into his tail feathers.

*Peace of mind: restored.*

-

Song Yu lowered his gaze to the porcelain dish. The bird food inside remained completely untouched, without the slightest sign of having been eaten.

He pulled out a chair, sat down, and looked up at the little bird on his finger, his expression exceedingly indifferent.

Bai Linlin was in the middle of twisting around to inspect his tail feathers when he turned back—only to lock eyes directly with the youth.

The bird jumped in fright, nearly tipping over backward.

"I really can't keep you alive, can I?"

Song Yu's voice lacked any emotional rise or fall. He had already researched the reasons for parrot anorexia; ruling out physical illness, it came down to emotional issues.

Depression, anxiety...

Dissatisfaction with its current situation.

A sharp, stabbing pain throbbed inside his wrist, causing his fingers to tremble slightly. Song Yu frowned. He had clearly taken his medication already.

The youth originally intended to withdraw his hand.

However, the moment the bird sensed his intention, tiny claws clamped tightly onto his finger.

"..."

With no alternative, Song Yu held still, using his left hand to pull out his phone and message Qi Siyang.

The phone screen flickered with light—looks like a reply came through.

Bai Linlin hadn't fully processed the situation yet. He simply felt that as an evolved bird, there was zero need for him to eat that bland bird food.

As for whether he could be kept alive or not...

Bai Linlin complained internally: *Why is this teenager so prone to overthinking things?* He hopped around on Song Yu's hand, but his claws accidentally snagged the youth's sleeve, causing the fabric to bunch upward.

The wrist was exposed.

Scars—blade marks, stacked one over another—marred the skin.

The bird froze.

Song Yu was looking down at his phone and hadn't noticed his sleeve snagging. However, the instant he finished his business and looked up—

Bai Linlin immediately used his claws to hook the fabric back down, covering it up tight and snug.

With a fluffy, rounded head, the bird turned his head away, standing in an exceptionally textbook posture, looking for all the world like a wind-up bird on a music box.

"..."

Song Yu had initially wanted to say something, but then felt he was truly sick—actually entertaining the thought of talking to a bird.

It couldn't understand anyway.

Keeping his right hand motionless, he watched the blue-feathered bird preen its feathers, using his hand entirely as a perch.

Until the phone buzzed with a vibration.

宋郁只好把视线移开，抬手拿过来手机，修长的手指在屏幕上滑动着，是齐思扬的回复：

【不吃饭吗？那也有可能生病了，我养恐怕也没时间。】

【这样，我有个师弟很爱鸟，我过去把它接走？】

大约一两秒后。

【但我还是觉得厌食应该不至于，白天我看小鸟精神状态挺好的。】

【你再观察观察，它或许偷吃东西了，应该是挑食吧。】

与此同时。

白粼粼终于松了一口气，怎么一直看他，这孩子心理肯定有点问题，不然手腕怎么……

啧，这有什么不开心的。

这有钱有颜的，多爽啊。

不像他一个二十多岁社畜，还没来得及谈恋爱，就——

“啾啾！！”

鸟惊恐，身子被少年修长的手指圈住，入目而来的是一张优越的面庞，靠近。

白粼粼圆滚滚的脑袋被揉搓了下，肉色的短喙被轻而易举地拨开了点，也正是因为这个动作，脸颊两侧的绒毛露出来点。

宋郁动作停顿了下，面色有些轻微的……茫然。

因为那绒毛上沾了点褐色的汤汁，散发着一股……

卤肉的味道。

作者有话说：

粼粼：难道我就是万里挑一的小鸟！
